jobs.title: Sr. Program Manager - TRACK
jobs.location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description
Location: Warren, MI or Austin, TX strongly preferred. If remote, candidate must be located in Eastern or Central time zones.

We are looking for a Senior Program Manager, to work at the intersection of strategy, operations, and project management with a focus on our intern, track and co-op programs across the United States. The person in this role will identify and drive strategic initiatives. We are seeking someone with demonstrated experience in the design, implementation, and execution of transformation programs as well as deep experience in partnership with clients/the business. The key to this role is to collaborate with multiple stakeholders to influence intern, track and co-op processes / programs through use of data and insights. Our ideal candidate is someone who can drive change across multiple teams and functions and influence them to work towards a shared goal.

Sr. Program Manager, Early Career Programs
- Lead operational and strategic initiatives across the Early Career Programs Team
- Partner with business leaders to define strategy and then build roadmaps and execution plans in service of the overall strategy
- Drive consistency across the internship experience throughout multiple locations within the US
- Ensure clear connection between strategy and functional operations to meet goals
- Collaborate with team members as well as cross-functional partners to identify process improvement opportunities; create solutions to address them
- Leverage quantitative and qualitative methodologies to make decisions and recommendations to drive improvements to our program
- Develop and maintain strong relationships with internal stakeholders
- Help build and develop training for intern managers within assigned function(s)
- Help Build and design intern project plan deliverables
- Seek to understand what key programming is necessary to make for a rewarding programmatic experience.
- Partner with key stakeholders to create a smooth onboarding and offboarding experience for interns, Track Participants and Co-Op students in all functions and locations
- Drive connectivity between our experiences; build a deeper connection to GM through innovative events and initiatives

Minimum Qualifications:
- BA/BS degree
- 6+ years of project management experience across multiple workstreams and functions
- 6+ years working with early career/ co-op / college / university programs
- Experience translating business challenges and questions into solutions
- Strategic, analytical and problem-solving skills
- Experience in designing and scaling detailed regular insights and updates out to a wide range of stakeholders
- Experience engaging directly with executive-level clients and stakeholders

Preferred Qualifications:
- Experience designing processes and experiences in an organization scaling for growth
- Experience managing complex programs across multiple functions and locations

Benefit options include medical, dental, vision, Health Savings Account, Flexible Spending Accounts, retirement savings plan, sickness and accident benefits, life insurance, paid vacation & holidays, tuition assistance programs, employee assistance program, GM vehicle discounts and more.

jobs.title: Staff Program Manager, AV PMO
jobs.location: Sunnyvale, California, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description
At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard — from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features. Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale.

ABOUT THE TEAM

At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. We create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. From breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design and next-generation safety, we’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard.

You will join the Autonomous Vehicle (AV) Program Management Office (PMO), a core pillar responsible for driving launch readiness for AV and ADAS features across L1–L4 autonomy. Based in the heart of Silicon Valley and Michigan, our team bridges the gap between cutting-edge software innovation and world-class automotive manufacturing, driving GM’s mission of Zero Crashes, Zero Congestion.

THE ROLE

As a Staff Program Manager for the next generation of Super Cruise, you will be the primary orchestrator for the evolution of GM’s flagship autonomous driving technology. Operating out of our Michigan or Sunnyvale hubs, you will act as the critical link between Product Management, Technical and Vehicle Program Management, Software Engineering, Hardware Engineering, Systems Engineering, Safety, Design and all other internal stakeholders to drive the strategic goals of the AV organization.

This is a high-visibility role. You aren't just tracking tasks; you are ensuring seamless coordination across all involved teams in order to drive high-quality milestone plans, navigate complex trade-offs, and ensure on-time execution of our most advanced safety-critical systems.

WHAT YOU'LL DO (RESPONSIBILITIES)

- Build trusting partnerships with Product, Program and Engineering leader s to synchronize Super Cruise development with hardware/software cycles and provide critical insights on program status, dependencies, and strategic trade-offs.

- Draft and track Program Milestones with clear success criteria, integrating guidance from Product Requirement Documents, Vehicle Program rollout plans, and company-wide software release schedules.

- Drive and coordinate progress towards major cross-functional program milestones in collaboration with Engineering Leads

- Own the Program Risk Register and coordinate the resolution of critical bottlenecks; proactively identify systemic risks early and facilitate the development of robust mitigation plans.

- Lead recurring Program, Risk, and Milestone Reviews while acting as a PMO SME to coach and guide peers on industry best practices, GM-specific processes and professional excellence.

- Manage the centralized Jira Align/Jira/Confluence ecosystem and facilitate the adoption of new operational rhythms to provide executive-level reporting and data-driven insights to senior leadership.

- Forecast resource needs and ensure all workstreams strictly comply with necessary standards and safety-critical software development practices.

- Ability to occasionally travel to Michigan or California locations if needed .

YOUR SKILLS & ABILITIES (REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS)

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering , Computer Science, or a related technical field.

- 10+ years of relevant experience in (Technical) Program Management or Engineering in the Tech, Automotive or Aerospace industry.

- 5+ years leading AV programs driving incremental delivery from inception to launch.

- Technical fluency in AV/ADAS platforms, including familiarity with AI-based driving models, simulation, validation, sensors, compute, infrastructure and operations.

- Expertise in agile and waterfall methodologies; fluent with tools like Jira, Jira Align, Confluence, and Microsoft 365.

- Experience working on software and hardware delivery within Automotive OEM vehicle development processes.

- Capacity to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and effectively manage competing priorities.

- Exceptional communication, interpersonal, and presentation skills with a proven track record of driving alignment among senior executive stakeholders and inspiring diverse, cross-functional teams to deliver change through influence without direct authority.

- Ability to travel and operate a motor vehicle on a regular basis.

WHAT WILL GIVE YOU A COMPETITIVE EDGE (PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS)

- Master’s degree in Engineering or MBA.

- Experience with Software-Defined-Vehicle architectures.

- Familiarity with systems engineering principles, validation cycles, and safety standards relevant to autonomous domains.

- Background in scaling operational systems and processes to support evolving technology roadmaps and launch targets.

- Understanding of GM’s GxDP (Global Vehicle/Software Development Process).

- Experience managing to GM’s VeSCoM (Vehicle Software Control Management) timing and Program Increments (PI).

- PMP, CSM, SAFe , Six Sigma, ISO 26262 or similar certifications

Hybrid:  This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to the Michigan or California office three times per week, at minimum.

Compensation:  The compensation information is a good faith estimate only. It is based on what a successful applicant might be paid in accordance with applicable state laws. The compensation may not be representative for positions located outside of the California Bay Area.

The salary range for this role is $134,700 to $245,000. The actual base salary a successful candidate will be offered within this range will vary based on factors relevant to the position.

Bonus Potential: An incentive pay program offers payouts based on company performance, job level, and individual performance.

Benefits:  GM offers a variety of health and wellbeing benefit programs. Benefit options include medical, dental, vision, Health Savings Account, Flexible Spending Accounts, retirement savings plan, sickness and accident benefits, life insurance, paid vacation & holidays, tuition assistance programs, employee assistance program, GM vehicle discounts and more.

Company Vehicle: Upon successful completion of a motor vehicle report review, you will be eligible to participate in a company vehicle evaluation program, through which you will be assigned a General Motors vehicle to drive and evaluate. Note: program participants are required to purchase/lease a qualifying GM vehicle every four years unless one of a limited number of exceptions applies.

jobs.title: Studio Engineering & Design Project / Program Management
jobs.description:
Job Description
Work Arrangement
These opportunities are categorized as on-site. Successful candidates are expected to work full time from the GM China Advanced Technical Center in Shanghai, China.

About GM China Design Studio
GM China Design Studio is both a production design studio and an advanced design studio. We shape meaningful vehicle experiences for GM brands serving customers in China and global markets, connecting near-term production programs with forward-looking exploration.
We are committed to creating an exceptional design environment where creativity, beauty, craftsmanship, and storytelling can thrive. Our teams work across disciplines and cultures to connect creative ambition with technical feasibility and coordinated delivery, helping transform design ideas into compelling vehicle experiences.

About This Evergreen Requisition
This evergreen requisition is established for talent pipelining purposes. GM China Design Studio is building a long-term pipeline of talent in Studio Engineering, Vehicle Packaging and Design Feasibility, and Design Project / Program Management to support current and anticipated business needs.
We welcome exceptional talent from around the world who are interested in contributing to production programs and advanced design exploration in our China studio. Opportunities may range from developing engineering studies or coordinating project deliverables to independently owning technical integration or complex design programs, depending on experience and business needs.
This posting covers related specialisms rather than a single role requiring expertise in every discipline. Candidates may specialize in studio engineering or project/program management; experience across both is welcome but not required. Engineering opportunities are not limited to a particular interior component or vehicle domain. These are individual-contributor opportunities, and a project or program management title does not imply people-management responsibility.
When submitting your application, please include:
- An updated resume or CV, indicating your primary specialization, relevant vehicle domains, and project experience.
- Relevant project examples or supporting materials, where available, that explain your contribution, problem-solving approach, and outcomes. Engineering applicants may share technical studies or design-integration examples; project/program management applicants may share project summaries, delivery achievements, or process improvements. A creative design portfolio is not required.

Please ensure all materials exclude undisclosed, confidential, proprietary, or otherwise sensitive information, projects, or data belonging to employers or clients. Share only information you are authorized to disclose; a non-confidential summary of your experience is welcome where detailed work cannot be shared.
Our recruiting and design teams will review your materials. If your profile aligns with a current or future opportunity, a recruiter will contact you to discuss next steps. This is an ongoing talent pipeline, rather than a commitment to an immediate vacancy; contact timing will depend on business needs and relevant opportunities.
If you do not meet every element below, we still encourage you to apply. We value sound judgment, collaborative problem-solving, relevant specialist capabilities, and the potential to grow.

The Opportunity
Help bridge creative design, engineering feasibility, and program execution within GM China Design Studio’s broader design delivery and studio operations environment.
Studio Engineering opportunities focus on enabling design through vehicle packaging, architecture studies, technical integration, and surface feasibility. Assignments may span overall vehicle proportions and layouts, interiors, exteriors, body systems, closures, occupant accommodation, or other design-related interfaces. Your scope will reflect your expertise and the needs of the program, rather than an expectation to cover every domain.
Design Project / Program Management opportunities focus on coordinating the people, decisions, dependencies, and deliverables needed to progress advanced and production design programs. You may support individual workstreams or take ownership of integrated program delivery, helping teams balance design intent, timing, content, cost, and quality.
You will collaborate with relevant partners across creative design, digital and physical modeling, Studio Engineering, vehicle architecture, engineering, human factors, manufacturing, product planning, and program teams. Assignments may also involve global studios, regional teams, and joint-venture partners.

What You May Do
Responsibilities will be selected according to your specialization, experience, and assigned program. You are not expected to perform every activity listed below.
Studio Engineering, Vehicle Packaging & Design Feasibility
- Develop initial vehicle layouts, package proposals, and alternative concepts using inputs from design, planning, engineering, and architecture teams.
- Conduct engineering, packaging, and “what-if” studies to explore future vehicle concepts, proportions, architectures, and technology integration.
- Create or evaluate architectural criteria, key sections, general arrangement drawings, and layout studies to support design development in relevant vehicle domains.
- Assess design surfaces and proposed solutions against applicable engineering, human-factors, performance, manufacturing, and regional requirements while protecting design intent.
- Investigate packaging conflicts, interferences, space limitations, and performance constraints; develop alternatives and communicate their implications for design, feasibility, and customer experience.
- Support the technical development of digital models, scale and full-size physical models, seating or package mock-ups, customer-research properties, and virtual or mixed-reality evaluations.
- Balance regional and global requirements with brand needs, architectural constraints, competitive references, and cost considerations.
- Coordinate technical studies and issue resolution with relevant specialists, tracking decisions and escalating unresolved trade-offs when appropriate.
- Prepare and present engineering studies, recommendations, and technical risks in studio reviews and cross-functional program discussions.

Design Project / Program Management
- Develop or maintain project plans, milestones, deliverables, dependencies, and action tracking for assigned advanced or production design work.
- Coordinate delivery across design, modeling, engineering, and program partners, supporting on-time completion and agreed quality expectations.
- Maintain alignment with approved program scope, content, architecture, targets, and timing; coordinate changes and make their impact visible to decision-makers.
- Represent design priorities in cross-functional discussions and communicate program requirements objectively within the studio.
- Track progress, anticipate risks and upcoming studio needs, and coordinate issue resolution or timely escalation with accountable partners.
- Facilitate studio operating meetings, cross-functional alignment sessions, milestone reviews, and leadership design reviews, with clear decisions, owners, and follow-through.
- Coordinate design-property and model-development needs with modeling and studio teams, supporting accurate forecasts of upcoming review assets and deliverables.
- Translate ambiguous or non-standard assignments into practical work packages, review points, and achievable milestones.
- Support discussions on timing, content, cost, and quality by clarifying options, dependencies, and consequences.
- Improve planning, reporting, meeting, and change-control practices to make program status clearer and delivery more efficient.

Contributions Shared Across Specialisms
- Help teams balance creative ambition with customer needs, technical feasibility, craftsmanship, quality, and delivery commitments.
- Build productive relationships across functions and influence outcomes through clear reasoning and collaboration rather than direct authority.
- Communicate progress, assumptions, trade-offs, and risks clearly, tailoring materials to technical, creative, and leadership audiences.
- Apply structured problem-solving while remaining adaptable in a fast-paced environment with evolving requirements.
- Follow applicable development processes and contribute improvements to tools, handoffs, and working practices.
- Share knowledge and, where appropriate, provide peer guidance without formal supervisory responsibility.
- Protect confidential design and program information throughout collaboration, reporting, and presentation.

What You May Bring
We welcome different career paths and levels of experience. The capabilities below describe potential areas of fit, not a cumulative checklist. Depth in studio engineering or project/program management is valued; expertise in both is not required.
Foundations Across Specialisms
- Relevant education, training, or equivalent practical experience. Backgrounds may include engineering, automotive or product development, industrial design, project management, business, or a related discipline, depending on the role.
- Experience appropriate to the opportunity, gained through professional work, internships, academic projects, or relevant technical and delivery assignments.
- An interest in how creative design develops into feasible, high-quality products and how multidisciplinary teams achieve that outcome.
- Strong communication, presentation, and collaboration skills, including the ability to explain complex issues and work constructively across functions and cultures.
- Initiative, analytical judgment, attention to detail, and the ability to organize priorities, anticipate issues, and remain effective under time pressure.
- Familiarity with product-development milestones, review gates, or collaborative delivery practices. Prior experience with GM’s Global Vehicle Development Process (GVDP) or internal systems is helpful but not a prerequisite; willingness to learn applicable processes is important.

Relevant to Studio Engineering Opportunities
- Engineering education or equivalent relevant technical experience, with the depth needed for the assigned responsibilities.
- Capabilities in one or more areas such as vehicle architecture, packaging, attribute integration, interior or exterior engineering, body or closure systems, surface integration, or design feasibility.
- Experience using Siemens NX or comparable CAD tools to develop, assess, and communicate technical solutions, appropriate to the assignment.
- The ability to interpret design intent and engineering criteria, develop alternatives, and explain trade-offs at component, system, or vehicle level.
- Understanding of relevant requirements such as occupant accommodation, access, visibility, usable space, manufacturing feasibility, or system interfaces, according to your domain.
- Experience with key sections, general arrangement drawings, dimensional comparisons, or competitive vehicle analysis is valuable for relevant opportunities.
- Previous design-studio experience is advantageous, while relevant capabilities from vehicle development, engineering consultancies, suppliers, or adjacent technical environments are also welcome.

Relevant to Design Project / Program Management Opportunities
- Experience coordinating or managing projects, workstreams, or programs in automotive, design, engineering, product development, or another relevant multidisciplinary environment.
- Capabilities in planning, scheduling, dependency tracking, risk and issue management, change control, and progress reporting, appropriate to the role.
- The ability to facilitate productive meetings, clarify ownership, support decisions, and follow through on commitments without relying on direct reporting authority.
- An understanding of how design deliverables, models, reviews, and engineering activities interact within a development schedule, or transferable experience with comparable product-development processes.
- The ability to turn ambiguity into clear plans and anticipate delivery needs before they become urgent.
- Experience coordinating complex production programs or multiple concurrent workstreams is valuable for more experienced opportunities, but is not required for every role in this pipeline.

Experience and Ownership
- For developing or earlier-career opportunities: relevant foundations, learning agility, and the ability to complete defined technical studies or coordination activities with appropriate guidance.
- For experienced or senior opportunities: the ability to independently own technical integration or project/program delivery within your specialization, resolve complex cross-functional issues, and provide clear recommendations to stakeholders.

We do not apply a single fixed years-of-experience threshold across this talent pipeline. The expected technical depth, program complexity, and level of independence will depend on the position. Prior people-management experience is not required.

Why Join GM China Design Studio
Connect advanced exploration with production impact in an internationally connected studio. Whether your strength is solving engineering challenges or coordinating complex design delivery, you can help preserve creative intent and turn ambitious vehicle concepts into achievable outcomes.
We welcome exceptional specialists and cross-disciplinary professionals at different stages of their careers. Your experience, judgment, and potential may align with an opportunity even if your background does not map perfectly to every item in this description.

At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard —from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.

Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale.

The Role
Global Manufacturing Electrical & SDV is looking for innovators who thrive in tough challenges and are passionate about tackling meaningful work that will shape the future of the automotive industry. This isn't a role for those looking for an easy path. It's for those who embrace change, push through obstacles, and take ownership of complex problems. While there will be long days and moments that test your resilience, you'll find purpose in your work, flexibility to prioritize your family, and the support of a people-first culture.
If you're ready to grow, thrive, and make a real impact, we'd love to hear from you.

This Role Is Ideal For
Program managers who enjoy leading complex initiatives, aligning diverse stakeholders, and driving operational outcomes across manufacturing environments. You'll thrive in this role if you can bring structure to ambiguity, influence without authority, and help teams deliver critical business objectives.
WHY
Help improve the quality and reliability of GM vehicles by supporting defect prevention, warranty reduction, and Electrical First Time Quality (EFTQ). Your work will directly support vehicle launches, manufacturing readiness, and the successful implementation of electrical systems across GM's global manufacturing network.
WHAT
As a Program Manager, Global Manufacturing Electrical & SDV, you will lead programs and strategic initiatives that support manufacturing operations, vehicle launches, and plant readiness activities. You will coordinate cross-functional teams, manage program execution, and drive measurable business outcomes across engineering, manufacturing, software, IT, quality, and operations organizations.
HOW
Partner with stakeholders across manufacturing, engineering, quality, software, IT, suppliers, and plant teams to execute program plans, manage risk, resolve issues, and ensure successful delivery of business objectives.

Work Arrangement – Onsite
The successful candidate is expected to report to the Warren Tech Center on a full-time basis.
This role requires up to 25% domestic and international travel.

This position may be filled with a Senior Program Manager or Program Manager. The level for this role will be determined based on the selected candidate's qualifications, skills, and experience.

Senior Program Manager Responsibilities
- Lead program strategy, scope, roadmap, timing, governance, dependencies, and delivery outcomes.
- Translate ambiguous and complex business challenges into actionable plans, decisions, and recovery strategies.
- Influence stakeholders across manufacturing, engineering, operations, software, IT, quality, supplier, and plant organizations.
- Drive readiness for vehicle launches, system deployments, testing activities, reflash events, traceability, and manufacturing solutions.
- Manage program health, risks, issues, dependencies, escalations, and corrective actions.
- Deliver executive-level communications that clearly articulate status, risks, decisions, and recommendations.

Program Manager Responsibilities
- Manage program plans, milestones, deliverables, dependencies, and execution activities.
- Coordinate cross-functional teams to ensure alignment on scope, timing, objectives, and deliverables.
- Support manufacturing readiness, launch activities, testing events, system implementations, and operational initiatives.
- Track and communicate program status, risks, issues, dependencies, and mitigation plans.
- Facilitate stakeholder discussions, issue resolution, and decision-making processes.
- Identify opportunities to improve program execution, team collaboration, and operational effectiveness.
- Deliver clear and concise updates to stakeholders and leadership.

Senior Program Manager Required
- 5+ years of program management, project management, or related experience.
- Demonstrated success leading complex programs, projects, or major workstreams in cross-functional environments.
- Experience developing and managing integrated plans, milestones, deliverables, dependencies, risks, and issue registers.
- Strong ability to influence stakeholders and drive alignment across competing priorities.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including executive-level presentations and stakeholder engagement with attention to detail.
- Ability to operate independently while managing multiple priorities and deliverables.
- Experience mentoring or coaching team members.

Program Manager
- Experience supporting programs, projects, or workstreams in cross-functional environments and maintaining project plans, milestones, action registers, risks, and deliverables.
- Ability to effectively coordinate stakeholders and drive action across teams.
- Strong analytical, organizational, problem-solving skills and strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- Demonstrated attention to detail and follow-through.
- Desire to grow into broader program leadership responsibilities.

What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)
- Experience supporting manufacturing operations, plant readiness, vehicle launches, or implementation events.
- Experience working across manufacturing engineering, manufacturing electrical, software, IT, quality, operations, supplier, or product engineering organizations.
- Familiarity with PMO governance, stage-gate reviews, change management, risk management, and lessons learned processes.
- Experience managing complex cross-functional initiatives in a manufacturing environment.

jobs.description:
Job Description
The Role

As a Lead System Integration Engineer – Enterprise Transformation, you will design, build, and scale enterprise integrations and data pipelines that modernize how systems work together across General Motors. From the software and core IT side of the transformation, you will focus on connecting Google Workspace, SaaS platforms, enterprise AI tools, and GM’s core business systems through secure, reusable, and scalable integration patterns.

This role is a strong fit for an experienced engineer who can independently deliver complex integration solutions, translate business and technical requirements into practical system designs, and build supportable, production-ready pipelines that align with enterprise standards. You will partner closely with product, engineering, technical program management, security, and business stakeholders to enable reliable data flow, workflow continuity, and platform interoperability across GM, while contributing reusable patterns that can be adopted broadly across the enterprise.

What You’ll Do

Strategic architecture and standards alignment
- Build reusable services, accelerators, and reference integration templates so transformation teams can solve repeatable connectivity needs more consistently.
- Apply enterprise platform guardrails by aligning integration designs with data standards, identity guidelines, and security policies.
- Partner with Security, Privacy, Identity, Information Lifecycle Management (ILM), and Retention teams to support workflows that process sensitive or regulated data.
- Evaluate incoming integration requests and recommend the appropriate technical path using approved platform capabilities, configuration options, or custom engineering.

Integration delivery and pipeline engineering
- Design, build, and maintain robust, resilient, and observable integrations using APIs, webhooks, scripts, connectors, and middleware services.
- Define source-to-destination data mappings, transformation logic, exception-handling patterns, and monitoring approaches that support reliable day-to-day operations.
- Modernize Microsoft-dependent workflows, legacy interfaces, and older automations into scalable, Google-aligned integration patterns.
- Connect Google Workspace with core GM platforms, including identity services, reporting environments, asset repositories, and approved AI platforms.
- Support end-to-end workflows that move data and trigger actions across enterprise systems.

Migration and coexistence engineering
- Design and support coexistence models that allow Microsoft, Google, and internal platforms to interoperate effectively during phased migration waves.
- Preserve workflow continuity where historical data, inactive-user content, or core systems must remain on legacy platforms during transition.
- Support cutover sequencing, permissions validation, metadata mapping, and post-deployment stabilization to reduce operational disruption.

Transformation pod engagement and sustainment
- Partner directly with transformation Product Leads and Technical Program Managers within business units to integrate Google capabilities into real-world operational processes.
- Provide technical leadership through design reviews, implementation guidance, and engineering best practices across the program.
- Author technical designs, dependency maps, operational runbooks, and handover materials that support long-term sustainment of integrated solutions.
- Support validation, troubleshooting, and hypercare activities during rollout and early adoption phases.

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications)

Core experience and education
- 7+ years of hands-on experience in integration engineering, software engineering, platform architecture, or enterprise application integration within complex enterprise environments.
- Strong systems-thinking capability, with proven experience mapping dependencies across applications, data layers, identity services, and business processes.
- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

Integration and software engineering proficiency
- Strong production-level proficiency in Python and core scripting or automation frameworks.
- Extensive experience building and supporting enterprise-grade integrations using REST APIs, webhooks, middleware solutions, and ETL or data transformation logic.
- Strong understanding of cloud-based integration patterns, modern application architecture, Git-based version control, and debugging integration issues across multi-system environments.
- Experience designing secure, supportable integrations across SaaS platforms and internal enterprise systems.

Security, identity, and cross-functional delivery
- Strong foundational knowledge of enterprise authentication, authorization, identity integration, and access-control frameworks.
- Proven history of working effectively with product managers, engineering teams, TPMs, security leads, and business stakeholders.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical tradeoffs, architecture risks, and engineering decisions to non-technical partners.

What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)
- Direct experience supporting large-scale Microsoft 365 to Google Workspace migration or coexistence programs.
- Familiarity with Google Workspace administration, Google Workspace APIs, Google Apps Script, and AppSheet.
- Experience connecting enterprise workflows to modern data and AI ecosystems such as Gemini Enterprise, Glean, AskGM, and Databricks.
- Familiarity with corporate data retention, ILM, privacy frameworks, and regulated data controls in large-scale enterprise environments.
- Experience supporting automated testing, cutover planning, data validation, hypercare support, and long-term sustainment models.

We are looking to fill two positions within the Digital Business Transformation Supply Chain team as we embark on transforming our legacy materials management and procurement processes and systems. This role will bridge business and IT teams in support of the SAP S/4HANA ecosystem deployment within Global Purchasing & Supply Chain (GPSC).

As the Senior Manager of Digital Business Transformation, you will help GPSC identify, evaluate, and implement new ideas, applications, and processes that improve organizational performance. This includes significant cross-functional engagement with GPSC functional areas and IT.  The focus of this role is creating and executing Master Data governance for this project.

- Collaborate with business and IT partners on innovation initiatives that align with GPSC’s business strategy and priorities.

- Apply critical thinking and creative problem-solving to explore alternative solutions and recommend the most effective approaches.

- Foster a culture of innovation by continuously learning new methodologies, tools, and best practices and sharing them across the organization.

- Partner with business owners and IT to define, document, and prioritize business requirements for SAP-enabled solutions and process changes.

- Develop KPIs and metrics that monitor roadmap progress, process adoption, data quality, and business outcomes, and communicate insights through concise, informative materials for leadership.

jobs.title: 2027 Summer Intern – Business Operations & Cost Optimization, Cadillac Racing Program Management
jobs.location: Milford, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description
The Role:
Join the Cadillac Racing Program Management team as a Business Operations & Cost Optimization Intern supporting trackside and race-event operations. You will audit spend and processes, analyze budget-to-actual performance, and identify cost-cutting opportunities that improve efficiency, cost visibility, and business control without compromising performance, safety, or race readiness.

The Team:
Cadillac Racing competes at the highest levels of global endurance racing, including the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship and FIA World Endurance Championship. The Sportscar Program Management team coordinates the people, partners, budgets, and operations required to compete successfully. This role supports that team by strengthening financial discipline, operational efficiency, and measurable cost-reduction initiatives across the program.

What You’ll Do:
- Create a program spend baseline by organizing historical and forecasted costs across selected race-event, logistics, purchasing, travel, freight, equipment, hospitality, and operational activities.
- Conduct structured audits of processes and transactions to identify cost drivers, duplication, control gaps, compliance issues, and opportunities for improvement.
- Review budgets, invoices, purchase orders, forecasts, and actuals; reconcile discrepancies and organize findings into clear, actionable summaries.
- Build Excel-based analyses, dashboards, audit tools, and status reports that help Program Management leadership monitor spending, efficiency, and implementation progress.
- Quantify potential savings, develop a prioritized cost-reduction pipeline, and support business cases for approved cost-cutting measures.
- Present audit findings and recommendations to Program Management leadership, then help track actions, owners, timing, and realized savings through implementation.
- Assess inventory-control practices for trackside parts, spares, consumables, and equipment; reconcile records to actual usage and identify opportunities to reduce excess, obsolete, or duplicate inventory.

Required Qualifications:
- Currently pursuing a Master’s degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Data Analytics, Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
- Expected to graduate between December 2027 and May 2029.
- Able to work full-time, 40 hours per week during the summer months.
- Strong analytical, auditing, problem-solving, and process-improvement skills, with the ability to translate detailed data into practical business recommendations.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, with the ability to organize data, build clear analyses, identify trends, and communicate recommendations effectively.
- Excellent communication, presentation, organization, and attention-to-detail skills, with the ability to work independently and across cross-functional teams.

Preferred Qualifications:
- Experience with process auditing, cost accounting, budgeting, variance analysis, procurement controls, Lean or Six Sigma, continuous improvement, or business-case development.
- Experience with financial or operational modeling, Power BI, dashboards, data visualization, or other analytical tools.
- Experience in automotive, motorsports, manufacturing, supply chain, event operations, or a similarly fast-paced environment.
- Experience developing executive-ready recommendations, presenting findings to leaders, or coordinating implementation across cross-functional teams or external partners.

GM does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. Do not apply for this role if you will need GM immigration sponsorship now or in the future. This includes direct company sponsorship, entry of GM as the immigration employer of record on a government form, and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (e.g., H1-B, OPT, STEM OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc.).

Work Arrangement:
Hybrid: This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to GM’s Milford Proving Ground in Milford, Michigan three times per week, at minimum, or at another frequency dictated by the business.

For those eligible, to help facilitate administration of relocation benefits, please apply using the permanent address you would move from.

Start dates for this internship role are May 24 and June 14, 2027.

jobs.title: Program Management Scheduling Lead - GPS
jobs.location: Pontiac, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description
At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard — from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features. Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale

Introduction:  In our pursuit to create a world with Zero Crashes, Zero Emissions, and Zero Congestion, GM’s global manufacturing engineering team is challenging the limits on what is possible and embracing agility as it reimagines how to build the next generation of vehicles. Our diverse team of manufacturing engineers play a crucial role in transforming our facilities through implementing the adoption of ground-breaking technologies. From raw sheet metal to final assembly, this team is reinventing the tools and processes that will enable GM to deliver on our promise to create an all-electric future.

Role Summary:
If you are interested in understanding the future of General Motors Propulsion products – engines, transmissions, and electric drive unit systems – GAIC (Global Artisan Innovation Center) GPS Scheduling has a place for you! This role is a “cross-functional” Leader role. Seeking a Scheduling Lead to own build scheduling, capacity planning, forecasting, and operating cadence for Assembly, Machining, and related laboratory and manufacturing activity. This role turns vehicle and dyno plans into executable schedules, leads cross-functional reviews, resolves priorities and escalations, maintains key business systems, and supports the people, safety, quality, and cost processes that keep the team running. Candidate will lead a diverse group of team members (contract, salary, third-party.)

(This role is on-site Daily)

Key Responsibilities :
- Develop and maintain short- and long-term operational schedules aligned with business priorities.
- Lead recurring planning and prioritization meetings; translate decisions into clear actions and schedule updates.
- Prepare regular performance reports; validate source data, reconcile results, and highlight key changes.
- Develop long-range forecasts, capacity plans, productivity outlooks, and resource requirements.
- Complete recurring operational and quality reporting using current plans, schedules, and actual results.
- Review schedules, resource constraints, priorities, and escalations and coordinate timely resolution of issues.
- Produce routine and ad hoc reports for stakeholders, maintain supporting procedures and documentation.
- Maintain shared business content and support system access, onboarding, updates, and approval workflows.
- Review and approve routine operational, administrative, and system-related requests.
- Lead team meetings and individual check-ins, support employee development, and coordinate recurring business activities.
- Support safety, quality, continuous-improvement, and standardized-work processes.
- Facilitate operational reviews, special initiatives, and collaboration across business functions.
- Present operating updates with clear risks, priorities, decisions, and follow-up actions.

Preferred Skills:
- Demonstrated experience in planning, scheduling, operations, or a closely related environment.
- Strong analytical skills with spreadsheets, forecasts, data reconciliation, and recurring performance reports.
- Ability to translate business plans, demand, constraints, and actual performance into practical short- and long-term plans.
- Experience leading cross-functional meetings, setting priorities, documenting decisions, and driving issues to resolution.
- Working knowledge of shared business platforms, system-access processes, and digital workflow tools.
- Clear written and verbal communication, sound judgment, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple deadlines, cross functionally.

Required
Education:  Bachelor’s degree in business/engineering related curriculum.

On Site:
This role is categorized as onsite. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to GM Pontiac Engineering Center, Building C on a full-time basis.

This job may be eligible for relocation benefits.

Onsite - This role is categorized as onsite. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to Rochester on a full-time basis.

The Role
We are seeking a skilled Manufacturing Engineer/Program Manager to support on going and launching products and programs.
This role will be part of the combined Program Management / Product Launch Team. This role may consist of launch or program management work.
The career level Manufacturing Program Manager, able to work autonomously with occasional guidance from supervision.  Skilled in sequence and flow of operations for the effective utilization of personnel, material, machines and facilities necessary for the production of parts.  Work is performed in a centralized manufacturing plant where creativity and initiative is exercised as well as independent judgement.

What You'll Do
- Individual contributor
- Lead, organize, follow, and ensure results for product changes throughout the lifecycle of the product
- Deliver launch milestones in accordance with Program Timing
- Drive Launch & Program level quality
- Ownership of respective product change review board & corresponding change leader duties (use of GM GMCH Teamcenter software)
- Coordinate all associated launch activities for respective programs following APQP, MQRR, and other GM specific launch processes.
- Ensure all launching and current products are complaint with GMS (GM Global Manufacturing System)
- Utilize advanced problem solving and continuous improvement tools to reduce cost (RedX, OpEx, etc.)
- Support the development and implementation of manufacturing processes, procedures, and documentation to improve efficiency, quality, and cost-effectiveness.
- Collaborate with multiple teams across the organization, in-person & virtually, to ensure manufacturability of new products and components.

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications)
- Bachelor's degree and 2+ years equivalent experience in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related field.
- Strong understanding and practical experience with various machining and assembly processes.
- Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot

What Can Give you a Competitive Advantage (Preferred Qualifications)
- Led capital equipment build projects with OEM partners while meeting schedule and budget targets.
- Proven experience in interpreting and utilizing blueprints and machine schematics.
- Ability to Addresses and evaluate a diverse range of issues using innovative methods and proposing alternative approaches.
